title: Channel page, Sales tab
summary: Diceroll's App Store channel page opened from Storefronts on its Sales tab: the storefront's one-line summary, the App Store SKUs with their offer and App Store Connect state, the 3.1.3(b) warning for an offer with no App Store SKU, recent App Store purchases, and the connection (derived app identity, verification key, store notifications) with restore under Advanced.
compare: It is the one channel page (A-22) with tabs Status, Releases, Listing, Sales and Setup; the Storefronts row lands on Sales. The crumbs say Storefronts › App Store and the Commerce sidebar entry stays active because that is where the person came from.
Sales renders only when the storefront side is set up; otherwise the same tab shows the storefront wizard with human steps only (commerce.sales-wizard).

The summary line reads 'Live  Selling 3 offers  412 purchases in 28 days  5 refunds  Test purchases off' as spaced items with no separator dots, so a wrapped line never starts with one; Live is green status text.

SKUs list each App Store product id in mono with its offer (name, then what it sells) and its App Store Connect state in Apple's own words (Ready for Sale, Waiting for Review). There is no price column: prices live on the offer. A row has no menu: the whole row opens its offer (chevron), where the App Store Connect deep link lives.
The 3.1.3(b) warning names the offer and why it matters and carries Create on App Store as its one action, which opens the L1 confirm (commerce.create-iap).
Import from App Store reads the store's in-app purchases and suggests offers; it is a button on the SKUs card, not a separate page.

Connection shows facts, never typed fields: the team key (from Platform → Store connections) and when it was last checked, the app identity read from the assigned app with 'Nothing to type', store notifications set up and verified with the last one received, and test purchases pointing at the one switch on Storefronts.

Restore policy is the only per-store option. It sits under Advanced, a closed disclosure that reads 'Advanced · Restoring purchases: App Store default'; opening it shows one labelled select (Restoring purchases: Follows the buyer's Apple account, the App Store default / Stays with the license) that saves on change.
Recent purchases are the Purchases ledger filtered to the App Store; a floating license (no account) shows the device; a refund is a danger pill.

Phone: the side column drops under the main column; both tables become stacked rows like Purchases, with nothing scrolling sideways: a SKU shows the mono id, then 'Offer · what it sells', then its App Store Connect state with its icon and a chevron; a recent purchase shows time, offer and state on one line and the account under it. The callout's action goes under its text.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: phone tables are stacked rows, Advanced is a closed disclosure and SKU rows open their offer; the warning tint is a brand token and is left to the brand package.

findings.issue: [phone] Both tables scroll sideways inside their cards; the App Store Connect state, the Offer column and the Recent purchases State (including Refunded) are off-screen with no cue, and 'Dice skins' wraps.
findings.resolution: Below 640px both tables render as stacked rows, as Purchases does: SKUs show the mono id, 'Offer · what it sells', then the App Store Connect state with a chevron; Recent purchases show time, offer and state on one line with the account under it. Nothing scrolls sideways. Compare item 10 updated.

findings.issue: [visual] Advanced's 'Change' floats beside three wrapped lines and Advanced is drawn always open; each SKU row has an unexplained '…' menu; the phone summary wraps so a dot starts line 2.
findings.resolution: Advanced is a closed disclosure ('Advanced · Restoring purchases: App Store default') that opens to one labelled select (in compare). The '…' menus are gone: each SKU row opens its offer, where the deep link lives. The summary uses spaced items with no separator dots.

findings.issue: [visual] The light warning callout fill (--pk-warning-subtle #eae7e6) reads grey-beige rather than amber.
findings.resolution: declined: the kit copies brand tokens verbatim from packages/brand (tools/mockups/build-kit.mjs regenerates them), so warming the token here would make the mockups disagree with the built console. The change belongs in @polaris-key/brand's tokens; flagged to the lead.
